pic.giza-pyramids.t: The pyramids of Giza seen from the desert: the Great Pyramid of Khufu, the pyramid of Khafre and the pyramid of Menkaure, built between about 2600 and 2500 BC.
pic.ziggurat-ur.t: The partly reconstructed Great Ziggurat of Ur near Nasiriyah, Iraq, raised by Ur-Nammu in the twenty-first century BC; the upper tiers are gone and the lower stage was refaced in the 1980s.
pic.parthenon.t: The Parthenon on the Acropolis of Athens, built 447–432 BC under Pericles, from the north-west.
pic.teotihuacan.t: Teotihuacan from the top of the Pyramid of the Moon, looking down the Avenue of the Dead; the Pyramid of the Sun (c. AD 100) stands at the far left.
pic.hagia-sophia-1857.t: Hagia Sophia from the south-west, with the minarets added after 1453; a lithograph of 1857.
pic.hagia-sophia-interior.t: The nave of Hagia Sophia under Justinian’s dome of 537, with the great calligraphic roundels of the Ottoman mosque.
pic.taj-mahal.t: The Taj Mahal at Agra, the tomb Shah Jahan built for Mumtaz Mahal from 1632, seen across the gardens.
pic.timbuktu-sankore.t: The Sankore mosque of Timbuktu, a fourteenth-century centre of learning, on a postcard of about 1905 from Edmond Fortier’s series.
pic.timbuktu-barth-1853.t: Timbuktu seen from a distance as Heinrich Barth’s party approached it on 7 September 1853; an engraving from Barth’s Reisen und Entdeckungen (Gotha, 1858).
pic.great-zimbabwe.t: Inside the Great Enclosure of Great Zimbabwe, the drystone walls raised between the eleventh and fifteenth centuries.
pic.dome-of-the-rock-1914.t: The mosaics and Quranic inscriptions inside the Dome of the Rock, built 691–692 under Abd al-Malik; a photograph published in 1914.
pic.borobudur-1913.t: A terrace of Borobudur, the ninth-century Buddhist monument in central Java, with its perforated stupas and relief panels; photographed in 1913.
pic.machu-picchu.t: Machu Picchu, the fifteenth-century Inca estate above the Urubamba, with Huayna Picchu rising behind the terraces.
pic.cederberg-san-elephants.t: San rock painting near Stadsaal in the Cederberg, South Africa: a line of men and a herd of elephants, painted perhaps around 5500 BC.
pic.venus-of-willendorf.t: The Venus of Willendorf, a limestone figurine about 11 cm high carved some 25,000 years ago, found in Austria in 1908 (a museum copy).
pic.narmer-palette.t: The Narmer Palette, both faces: the siltstone ceremonial palette of about 3100 BC on which the king wears the crowns of Upper and of Lower Egypt.
pic.nefertiti-bust.t: The bust of Nefertiti, made in Thutmose’s workshop at Amarna about 1345 BC; this is the museum replica at the Rosicrucian Egyptian Museum, San José, the original being in Berlin.
pic.hagia-sophia-vestibule-mosaic.t: The Virgin and Child between Justinian, offering the church, and Constantine, offering the city: the mosaic of about 1000 over the south-west vestibule door of Hagia Sophia.
pic.alexander-mosaic.t: Alexander on Bucephalus at the battle of Issus: detail of the Alexander Mosaic from the House of the Faun at Pompeii, laid about 100 BC after a Greek painting.
pic.gladiator-mosaic.t: The retiarius Kalendio against Astyanax: a Roman gladiator mosaic of the third century AD, with the inscriptions that record Astyanax’s victory.
pic.huizong-auspicious-cranes.t: Auspicious Cranes, the handscroll Emperor Huizong painted and inscribed in 1112 to record the flock of cranes seen over the palace gate.
pic.black-death-tournai-1353.t: The citizens of Tournai bury their plague dead in 1349: a miniature from Gilles li Muisis’ Antiquitates Flandriae, made about 1353.
pic.dance-of-death-1493.t: The Dance of Death: Michael Wolgemut’s woodcut in Hartmann Schedel’s Nuremberg Chronicle of 1493, the image of mortality the plague left to Europe.
pic.hadrians-wall.t: Hadrian’s Wall at Milecastle 39 (Castle Nick), looking east along the Whin Sill; the wall was begun in AD 122.
pic.versailles-treaty-1919.t: Signing of the Treaty of Versailles, 1919, by John Christen Johansen: Wilson seated near the centre among the delegates in the Hall of Mirrors.
pic.mongol-invasion-japan-1274.t: The samurai Takezaki Suenaga charges Mongol archers and a bursting bomb at Hakata in 1274: a scene from the Mōko Shūrai Ekotoba scroll, painted about 1293.
pic.scheveningen-1653.t: The battle of Scheveningen (Ter Heijde), 10 August 1653, the last battle of the first Anglo-Dutch war: Willem van de Velde the Elder’s pen painting of 1657.
pic.san-martin-andes-1817.t: San Martín and O’Higgins crossing the Andes in January 1817 to free Chile, painted by Julio Vila y Prades in the late nineteenth century.
pic.sekigahara-1600.t: The battle of Sekigahara, 21 October 1600, on a nineteenth-century folding screen: some 160,000 samurai fought for six hours.
pic.goya-third-of-may-1808.t: The Third of May 1808: Goya’s painting of 1814 of the French firing squads shooting the Madrid insurgents on the Príncipe Pío hill.
pic.bastille-1789.t: The storming of the Bastille and the arrest of its governor, de Launay, on 14 July 1789, painted by an unknown artist about 1790.
pic.congress-of-vienna-1815.t: The Congress of Vienna: Jean-Baptiste Isabey’s group portrait of 1819, with Wellington at the far left, Castlereagh seated at the centre and Metternich standing before him.
pic.smallpox-florentine-codex-1520.t: Nahua victims of the smallpox of 1520, drawn in the Florentine Codex compiled under Sahagún in the 1570s: the sick lie covered in pustules while a healer attends them.
pic.cortes-march-codex-azcatitlan.t: Cortés’s army on the march with Malintzin at its head, from the Codex Azcatitlan, a Nahua pictorial history of the late sixteenth century.
pic.benz-motorwagen-1885.t: The Benz Patent-Motorwagen of 1885–86, the first motor car offered for sale, in a photograph of 1885.
pic.tsarskoye-selo-railway-1837.t: The first train arriving at Tsarskoye Selo on the Tsarskoye Selo Railway, Russia’s first, opened in 1837; a lithograph of the 1840s.
pic.nicopolis-1396.t: The battle of Nicopolis, 25 September 1396, in an Ottoman miniature of 1523: Bayezid’s army on the left routs the crusader knights.
pic.theodosian-walls.t: The Theodosian walls of Constantinople, built from 413: the inner wall on the right, the outer wall on the left, with the moat beyond.
pic.jericho-tower.t: The stone tower of Neolithic Jericho, about 8.5 m high and built around 8000 BC, one of the oldest monuments in the world.
pic.hammurabi-stele.t: The stele of Hammurabi, the basalt column of about 1750 BC found at Susa in 1901, with the king before the sun-god Shamash above the 282 laws.
pic.ashoka-pillar-allahabad.t: The Allahabad pillar of Ashoka, inscribed with his edicts in the third century BC, photographed by Thomas Rust in the nineteenth century.
pic.death-of-socrates-david.t: The Death of Socrates, Jacques-Louis David’s painting of 1787: Socrates reaches for the hemlock while his pupils grieve.
pic.burning-of-persepolis-rochegrosse.t: The burning of Persepolis in 330 BC as Georges Rochegrosse imagined it in 1890: Thaïs, torch in hand, carried by Alexander’s revellers.
pic.clovis-point.t: A Clovis point from Utah, between 11,000 and 13,000 years old, the fluted spearhead of the first widespread culture of the Americas.
pic.cahokia-monks-mound.t: Monks Mound at Cahokia, completed about 1100, the largest earthen mound in North America, some 30 m high.
pic.mesa-verde-cliff-palace.t: Cliff Palace at Mesa Verde, the Ancestral Puebloan cliff town begun about 1190 and abandoned by 1300.
pic.olmec-colossal-head.t: An Olmec colossal head of basalt, carved between about 1200 and 900 BC, in the Museo de Antropología de Xalapa.
pic.nazca-condor.t: The Condor of the Nazca lines, scraped into the desert floor of southern Peru between about 200 BC and AD 600.
pic.diamond-sutra-868.t: The frontispiece of the Diamond Sutra printed in China on 11 May 868, the oldest dated printed book, found at Dunhuang in 1907.
pic.stalingrad-1942.t: Soviet soldiers fighting from the ruins of a bombed building in Stalingrad in 1942.
pic.pearl-harbor-1941.t: Pearl Harbor from a Japanese aircraft on 7 December 1941, minutes into the torpedo attack on Battleship Row.
pic.petrograd-february-1917.t: Soldiers and demonstrators in Petrograd during the February Revolution of 1917.
pic.berlin-airlift-1948.t: Berliners watch a US Air Force C-54 come in to land at Tempelhof during the airlift of 1948.
pic.world-trade-center-2001.t: Rescue workers on the rubble of the World Trade Center on 19 September 2001, the flag flying over the debris.
pic.ypres-1916.t: The ruined Grote Markt of Ypres in 1916, after two years on the Western Front.
pic.catalan-atlas-caravan-1375.t: A caravan on the Silk Road from the Catalan Atlas of 1375, drawn in Majorca by Cresques Abraham.
pic.peter-the-hermit-1095.t: Peter the Hermit preaching the First Crusade, as an illustrator of Cassell’s History of England imagined it in the early twentieth century.
pic.vienna-siege-1529.t: Vienna during the Ottoman siege of 1529, with St Stephen’s at the centre: detail of the panoramic woodcut map made the following year.
pic.landing-of-columbus-bierstadt.t: The Landing of Columbus, Albert Bierstadt’s ten-foot canvas of 1893, the romantic American image of 12 October 1492.
pic.brooks-slave-ship-1788.t: The stowage plan of the slave ship Brooks, printed by the abolitionists in 1788 and reprinted for decades.
pic.copernicus-heliocentric-1543.t: The heliocentric diagram from Copernicus’s De revolutionibus orbium coelestium, printed at Nuremberg in 1543.
pic.great-famine-1315.t: Death astride a manticore and Famine pointing to her mouth: a manuscript illumination made at Erfurt at the time of the Great Famine of 1315–17.
pic.napoleon-crossing-alps-david.t: Napoleon Crossing the Alps, Jacques-Louis David’s portrait of 1801–05 of the First Consul on the Great St Bernard in May 1800 (the Malmaison version).
pic.dardanelles-gun.t: The Dardanelles Gun, the bronze bombard cast for Mehmed II in 1464 on the pattern of the guns that breached Constantinople in 1453.
pic.istanbul-lorck-1559.t: The Fatih mosque above the roofs of Istanbul, from Melchior Lorck’s panorama of the city drawn in 1559.
pic.moai-rano-raraku-1914.t: Standing moai on the outer slope of Rano Raraku, buried to the shoulders, photographed by the Mana expedition of Katherine and William Scoresby Routledge in 1914.
pic.moai-head-rano-raraku-1914.t: The heads of two moai on Rano Raraku, the ear lobes carved as ropes; a photograph of the Routledge expedition of 1914.
pic.chichen-itza-castillo-catherwood-184: The Castillo of Chichén Itzá, overgrown, as Frederick Catherwood drew it in 1842: engraving 51 in Stephens’s Incidents of Travel in Yucatan (New York, 1843).
pic.cordoba-mosque-1873.t: The forest of horseshoe arches of the Great Mosque of Córdoba, begun by Abd al-Rahman I in 785: a wood engraving in Samuel Irenæus Prime’s The Alhambra and the Kremlin (New York, 1873).
pic.alhambra-from-generalife-1873.t: The Alhambra seen from the Generalife, the Nasrid palace-fortress of Granada built mainly in the fourteenth century: a wood engraving of 1873.
pic.kremlin-1873.t: The Kremlin of Moscow from across the Moskva, with the Great Stone Bridge, the Ivan the Great bell tower and the cathedrals: a wood engraving of 1873.
pic.potala-1904.t: The Potala above Lhasa, the palace of the Dalai Lamas rebuilt from 1645, photographed as the Younghusband expedition reached the city in August 1904.
pic.potala-west-front-1904.t: The west front of the Potala, Lhasa, photographed by the Younghusband expedition in 1904.
pic.versailles-garden-front-1919.t: The palace of Versailles, the Marble Court of Louis XIII’s hunting lodge enclosed by Louis XIV’s palace: a photograph in Francis Loring Payne’s The Story of Versailles (New York, 1919).
pic.versailles-hall-of-mirrors-1919.t: The Hall of Mirrors at Versailles, built by Mansart and painted by Le Brun in 1678–84, where the German Empire was proclaimed in 1871 and the treaty signed in 1919: a photograph of 1919.
pic.pantheon-rome-1914.t: The Pantheon of Rome, Hadrian’s temple of about AD 126 with its sixteen-column porch, still wearing the two bell towers removed in 1883; a photograph published in 1914.
pic.colosseum-1914.t: The Colosseum, the Flavian amphitheatre dedicated in AD 80, from the south-east; a photograph published in 1914.
pic.colosseum-interior-1914.t: The interior of the Colosseum with the excavated substructures of the arena; a photograph published in 1914.
pic.st-peters-1914.t: St Peter’s Basilica and its piazza from the east, Maderno’s façade of 1612 under Michelangelo’s dome; a photograph published in 1914.
pic.notre-dame-raffaelli-1902.t: Notre-Dame de Paris from the quai de la Tournelle, the apse and flying buttresses above the Seine, painted by Jean-François Raffaëlli in 1902.
pic.st-peters-wilson-1760.t: St Peter’s and the Vatican from the Janiculum, Richard Wilson’s view of Rome painted between 1757 and 1764.
pic.westminster-monet-fog-1904.t: The Houses of Parliament, Effect of Fog: Monet’s view of Barry and Pugin’s palace across the Thames, painted in 1904 from his London campaigns of 1899–1901.
pic.westminster-edwards-1878.t: The Thames at Westminster, with the Palace of Westminster and the clock tower above the river traffic, painted by Edwin Edwards in 1878.
pic.eiffel-tower-renoux-1922.t: The Eiffel Tower from the Trocadéro gardens, behind Frémiet’s bronze elephant, painted by Jules Ernest Renoux in 1922.
pic.eiffel-tower-delaunay-1911.t: Tour Eiffel, Robert Delaunay’s fractured tower of 1911, the modern Paris of the Orphists.
pic.parthenon-church-1871.t: The Parthenon, Frederic Edwin Church’s painting of 1871 from his journey to Athens in 1869, the ruin in the late light.
pic.giza-great-pyramid-dauzats.t: The Great Pyramid of Giza, its courses climbed by tiny figures, painted by Adrien Dauzats after his Egyptian journey of 1830.
pic.waterloo-pieneman-1824.t: The Battle of Waterloo, Jan Willem Pieneman’s vast canvas of 1824: Wellington at the centre, the wounded Prince of Orange carried off at the left, 18 June 1815.
pic.retreat-from-moscow-vereshchagin.t: On the High Road: Retreat, Flight. Napoleon walks with his staff through the snow during the retreat from Moscow, from Vasily Vereshchagin’s 1812 series of about 1890.
pic.trafalgar-stanfield-1836.t: The Battle of Trafalgar, 21 October 1805, painted by Clarkson Stanfield in 1836: the Victory in the thick of the fight.
pic.crusaders-before-jerusalem-kaulbach-: Crusaders before Jerusalem: Wilhelm von Kaulbach’s painting of 1860 of the army of the First Crusade at the sight of the city in June 1099.
pic.agincourt-gilbert-1884.t: Morning of the Battle of Agincourt, 25 October 1415: Henry V and his army before the fight, painted by Sir John Gilbert in 1884.
pic.liberty-leading-the-people-1830.t: Liberty Leading the People, Delacroix’s painting of the July Revolution of 1830, finished the same year.
pic.great-fire-of-london-1666.t: The Great Fire of London, September 1666, seen from a boat on the Thames with old St Paul’s and London Bridge in the blaze; an anonymous painting of the seventeenth century.
pic.paris-commune-boulanger-1871.t: An episode of the Commune, place de la Concorde: Gustave Boulanger’s painting of about 1871 of the fighting in Paris in May 1871.
pic.balaclava-jones-1854.t: The Conflict at the Guns, Balaclava: George Jones’s painting of 1854 of the Heavy Brigade among the Russian guns on 25 October 1854.
pic.execution-of-streltsy-surikov-1881.t: The Morning of the Execution of the Streltsy, Vasily Surikov’s painting of 1881: Red Square in October 1698, Peter the Great on horseback at the right.
pic.vercingetorix-royer-1899.t: Vercingetorix throws down his arms at the feet of Julius Caesar after Alesia, 52 BC: Lionel Royer’s painting of 1899.
pic.second-ypres-jack-1916.t: The Second Battle of Ypres, 22 April to 25 May 1915: Richard Jack’s painting of 1916 of the Canadian line under the first gas attack.
